description: When warren's supervisor calls Bun.spawn({ cmd: ['burrow', ...], cwd: '/app' }), Bun resolves 'burrow' via /app/node_modules/.bin/burrow BEFORE walking PATH. So a Dockerfile that 'bun install -g' a newer @os-eco/burrow-cli to /usr/local/bin/burrow has zero effect on the supervisor's spawned process — it runs the lockfile-pinned local copy. Bumping a CLI that warren both depends on (library) AND ships globally requires updating BOTH the Dockerfile pin AND package.json + bun.lock; otherwise the supervisor runs the stale local bin.
resolution: Bump @os-eco/burrow-cli (and any other dual-purpose CLI) in three places: Dockerfile global install line, package.json deps, and bun.lock (regenerate via 'bun install'). Verify post-rebuild: docker compose exec warren sh -c 'for pid in /proc/[0-9]*; do tr "\\0" " " < "$pid/cmdline"; done | grep burrow.serve' — if the path is /app/node_modules/.bin/burrow, the lockfile pin is what's running.

name: cli-plan-pl-882c
description: The 0.14 agent-facing CLI + npm publish plan is filed as pl-882c (parent seed warren-d089, 14 children). Canonical design source: docs/design/2026-07-29-planning-session-record.md §3 — owner decisions D1-D6 are locked there and restated in the plan context. Step 14 (warren-58dd) is where mx-834a3a (container-only distribution) gets formally superseded; do not publish to npm before that step runs. warren-53a7 (NDJSON parser merge) was deliberately left out of the plan because it conflicts with D2 (UI keeps its own HTTP client).

title: Warren CLI IS published to npm as @os-eco/warren-cli; supersedes mx-834a3a (container-only distribution)
rationale: Reversal of mx-834a3a. The old decision held when the CLI was server-internal (operated on local sqlite + burrow socket inside the container) with zero external consumers. Three things postdate it: (1) ROADMAP ring 1 requires npm install as a distribution channel for the agent-facing CLI; (2) the docker-build gate shipped, so image quality no longer depends on npm being absent; (3) pl-882c rebuilt the CLI onto HTTP (warren-97a2 D3 collapse, login/prime, generated reference), making agents the primary CLI consumer — a remote 'warren run' works from any laptop, so the old 'confusing failures outside the container' rationale no longer applies. The container image remains the canonical SERVER artifact; npm distributes only the CLI/SDK surface. Package ships raw bun-shebang TypeScript with engines.bun (fleet precedent @os-eco/burrow-cli, mx-be6bc5): files allowlist is ['src','!src/ui'] (UI source stays OUT of the tarball — it is a build-time workspace, not a runtime surface), publishConfig.access public, exports '.' + './client'. release.yml gains a publish job needs [release, deploy] so npm can never carry a version without its ghcr image.

description: First npm publish from release.yml failed with EOTP: a classic npm 'Publish' token cannot write when account 2FA covers writes — npm demands an interactive OTP, which CI cannot supply. The failure surfaced only at the final registry write, after auth, pack, and provenance signing all succeeded (release run 30926493113, v0.14.0).
resolution: Replace NPM_TOKEN with a granular access token (read/write, @os-eco scope) or a classic Automation token — both bypass the OTP requirement by design. Then 'gh run rerun <id> --failed' completes the chain: the idempotent publish re-runs and the skipped promote/announce dependents revive.

description: seeds-merge-autoheal.yml crashed on first firing: 'gh pr view $PR_NUMBER' ran before actions/checkout and without --repo, so gh aborted with 'not a git repository'. In GitHub Actions, every gh pr/api call must be repo-explicit (job-level GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }} env, or --repo flags) unless it runs after checkout.
resolution: PR #851 (warren-53bd): job-level GH_REPO env added; all gh calls repo-explicit. Verified green on the very next PR (#853).

name: update-branch-ratchet-overshoot
description: gh pr update-branch can push a green PR over a ratchet gate: when main and the branch both grew the same file (e.g. src/server/main/index.ts wiring), the update merge lands the sum (501>500 lines, check:size). Fix by dispatching a repair run on the PR branch that EXTRACTS a cohesive module (repo pattern: *-wiring.ts under src/server/main/) — never by raising file-size-budgets.json, whose ratchet only goes down.

name: gh-run-rerun-stale-merge-commit
description: Re-running a failed pull_request workflow (gh run rerun --failed) pins the stale merge commit computed at the original event, so a fix merged to main afterward is invisible to the rerun. To pick up a base-branch fix on a PR's CI, use 'gh pr update-branch <n>' instead — it pushes a merge of main into the branch and triggers fresh checks on a new merge ref. Used to land PR #964 after #965 fixed the red ci-postgres on main.
